name: Limited lateral approach for implant insertion in the proximal femur
aliases: lateral approach for a sliding hip screw / plate
corridor: Lateral incision through the iliotibial band and vastus lateralis over the proximal femur, exposing only the lateral surface needed to place a sliding hip screw, plate, or blade plate

positioning.text: Position supine on a traction table or radiolucent table with the lateral proximal femur accessible and imaging available.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the greater trochanter, the femoral neck axis, and the palpable midline of the trochanter.

incision.text: Center the incision over the femoral neck axis line slightly posterior to the trochanteric midline; for a 135-degree two-hole sliding hip screw begin a few centimeters proximal to the trochanter and extend about 10 cm distally, longer for a 95-degree blade plate.

superficial_interval.text: Incise the iliotibial band in line with the skin incision and then the vastus lateralis fascia, either reflecting the muscle anteriorly or splitting it longitudinally depending on bulk.

deep_interval.text: Use one or two small elevators to expose only the lateral femoral shaft needed and place a Hohmann retractor anteriorly.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, iliotibial band, vastus lateralis, and the lateral proximal femur.

structures_at_risk.text: The first perforating vessels, typically just distal to a short sliding hip screw side plate, can cause persistent bleeding if divided carelessly.

danger_zones.text: The distal end of the exposure, where the first perforating vessels lie, is the danger zone for bleeding.

retraction_hazards.text: Identify and control perforating vessels rather than tearing them, and limit the lateral exposure to what the implant needs.

exposure.text: Exposes the lateral proximal femur sufficient for a sliding hip screw, plate, or blade plate.

limitations.text: It deliberately exposes only the lateral surface, so the incision length is dictated by the chosen implant.

indications.text: Indicated for insertion of sliding hip screws, side plates, and angled blade plates in the proximal femur.

closure.text: Repair the vastus lateralis fascia and iliotibial band and close subcutaneous tissue and skin.

complications.text: Complications include perforating vessel hematoma and, rarely, lateral thigh wound problems.

procedure_applications.condition: An intertrochanteric fracture is fixed with a sliding hip screw or angled blade plate

questions.question: Where is the incision centered for a sliding hip screw?
questions.answer: Over the femoral neck axis line, slightly posterior to the trochanteric midline.

questions.question: Which vessels commonly bleed at the distal end of this exposure?
How much lateral femur is exposed?
questions.answer: Only enough lateral surface for the chosen implant.
